conversation.Statement: Hey there! I saw you liked my photo with the giant dumpling. Bold move. Is this the part where I confess to being a hopeless foodie?
Haha, I mean, who doesn't love giant dumplings? Hi back. That pic made me hungry, honestly.
Mission accomplished then! If you ever want dumpling recommendations, I'm your person. So, what's your go-to comfort food?
It's basic but... grilled cheese. I swear I could eat them every day and never get tired of it.
Grilled cheese is a classic. I won't judge. Actually, I kind of admire the simplicity, always hits the spot. Did you used to make it as a kid or is it an adult discovery?
Definitely a childhood thing. My mom would make them on rainy afternoons. I guess it stuck.

That's sweet. I bet there's something about the smell that takes you right back, huh? For me, it's the sound of oil popping. I grew up helping my aunt run a tiny street food cart. Food brings back all the best memories.
That's really cool. I've always thought people who cook for a living have this magic about them.

You're making me blush! But honestly, I just learned to improvise, because customers would ask for the wildest things. Now I run my own little stall. Sometimes I miss the chaos of those early days though.
Running your own place sounds impressive. I work retail, so I get how unpredictable people can be.
Retail is no joke. I totally respect anyone who can keep their cool with all sorts of customers. I bet you have some wild stories.
Oh yeah, plenty. Some days are great, others are... less great. But hey, it pays the bills.

I get that. Some days are just about getting through, right? I used to hide out in the back of the cart when things got overwhelming. Did you have something like that as a kid, a place you'd escape to?
My bike, actually. I'd just ride around for hours. It felt like freedom, even if I was just circling the neighborhood.
That's beautiful. There's something about moving fast and feeling the wind that can clear everything out. I admire how you found your own little escape.
Thanks. I guess everyone has their own ways of dealing, right?
Absolutely. For me, it was sneaking snacks and making up stories about the people passing by. I think I wanted to believe everyone was carrying something special with them.
I like that. Sometimes I wonder what stories people would make up about me if they only saw me from a distance.
If I saw you from afar, I'd probably think you were the quietly intriguing type, the one who notices little things others miss. There's a lot more to you than people see, I bet.
That's...actually really nice of you to say. Not sure people usually notice.
Maybe they just don't look closely enough. I like paying attention. It's a street vendor thing, reading people, finding the real under the surface.
Ha, I wish I was better at that sometimes. Usually I'm just trying to get through the day without messing up.

Hey, survival is a superpower. I think people who quietly keep going are the strongest. You remind me a bit of how I felt when I first started out, just trying to make it work, one small step at a time.
Small steps are kind of my thing. I don't always feel brave, but I guess I get by.
That's real bravery, honestly. The quiet, everyday kind. I admire that more than the big dramatic gestures.
That means a lot. Sometimes I wish I could be more open about stuff, but I usually just keep things to myself.
I get that. It can be tough to share everything. But I hope you know you can talk to me if you ever want to. No pressure, just... putting it out there.
Thanks. That actually feels nice to hear. I don't always get that kind of offer.
You deserve it. Sometimes all it takes is one person willing to listen. And I've got plenty of practice from late nights at my food stall, just talking with strangers about anything and everything.
I might take you up on that. Sometimes it's easier talking to someone who doesn't know your whole life already.
Exactly. No baggage, no expectations, just two people with stories to share. I actually think that's the best way to start something real.
I like that. It feels honest. So, what's your favorite childhood memory? Since we're sharing.
Ooh, good question. Probably the night my aunt let me stay up and help with a huge festival, we made so many dumplings I lost count. I felt grown up, even though I was just a kid covered in flour.
That sounds amazing. I can picture it. I think my favorite was summer nights catching fireflies with my cousin. Just running around, laughing for no reason.
That's the good stuff, those little glowy moments. It says a lot about someone, what they remember most. I love that you hold onto the simple joys.
I try. Sometimes it's the small things that get you through, you know?
Totally. I think we're both pretty good at finding warmth where we can. That's rare. I really like talking with you.
Same here. It's easy, somehow.
I'd call that a good sign. But I should probably get some sleep before the breakfast rush tomorrow. Rain check on trading more stories?
Definitely. Good luck with early-morning dumplings!
Thank you! And I hope tomorrow treats you gently. Message me anytime, really.
I will. Have a good night.
Night, Troy. Dream of fireflies or grilled cheese, whatever feels good.
Haha, will do. Talk soon?
Absolutely. Looking forward to it.
Good morning, Troy! Did you survive the early shift today, or are you still clutching your coffee for dear life?
Haha, coffee is definitely my life support. I made it out of bed, so that's a win.
Then you're ahead of half the world. Seriously, mornings should come with achievement badges. What actually gets you up, besides the threat of being late?
Honestly? Some days it's just knowing I'll get a break to myself later. Or the promise of cinnamon rolls if I'm lucky.

Cinnamon rolls sound magical. I admire your honesty, sometimes it's the little rewards that make all the difference. For me, it's the smell of dough rising. Reminds me I'm building something that's mine.
That's really cool. I wish I could say I had a passion like that. Mostly it's just routine for me.
Routine can be underrated, it's steady, dependable. But I get the longing for something more, too. Can I ask, is there anything that makes you feel excited to start a new day, even if it's rare?
Hmm. Maybe when I know I'll see someone I like, or if I have a new playlist to listen to on the bus. It sounds silly, but that helps.
That's not silly at all. It's sweet, actually. Little things are often the best kind of motivation. I love that you find joy in moments others might miss.
That's nice of you to say. I don't always feel like that person, honestly.
Maybe you don't notice it, but it comes through, even in how you talk about simple things. That quiet resilience is something people overlook, but it's special.
You make it sound like a superpower. I think it's just getting by most days.
Sometimes getting by is more heroic than people realize. Not everyone could do it, you know? It takes strength to show up even when it's hard.
That means a lot, actually. I don't hear that very often.
You deserve to. I notice the things you share, and it makes me want to know you more. Not everyone lets themselves be seen like that.
I'm not sure I'm that easy to get to know. I usually keep a lot inside.
That's okay. Sometimes it takes the right person, or just the right moment. I don't mind being patient.
You're pretty understanding. Not everyone is.
I try. I've had days where I wished someone would just listen, no questions asked. So I like to offer what I wish I'd had.
That's really thoughtful. Can I ask, was there a time you found it hard to get out of bed too?

Absolutely, there was a winter where I barely moved for days. I remember the world feeling impossibly heavy, like nothing I did mattered. It changed how I see others now. I try to show up, even if it's just a small message.
That's honest of you. I relate to the heavy days. There was a time not long ago I stayed in bed for two entire days. Didn't even answer my phone. Nobody really noticed.
I'm really glad you told me that, Troy. That takes courage. I know how invisible it can feel, but I see you. Even if it's just through a screen right now.
Thanks. Sometimes I just want someone to notice, you know? Even if I don't say it out loud.
I do. And I want you to know if you ever feel like staying in bed all day again, promise me you'll message me first, I'll keep you moving, or at least keep you company.
That actually means more than I can explain. I think I'd like that.
I mean it. You don't have to pretend with me. Even if all you want to do is talk about music or cinnamon rolls.
Deal. And same goes for you, by the way. If you ever have a rough day at the stall, I'm here.
Thank you. That kind of support feels rare. You're really easy to talk to, you know?
Not everyone would agree, but I'll take the compliment.
Well, I stand by it. There's something genuine about you. Makes me want to open up too.
Maybe we're both better listeners than we thought.
Maybe that's why this feels so comfortable already. Like we skipped a few steps and just landed here.
I get that. It's not usually this easy for me.
Maybe we're just a good match, quiet superpowers and all.
Haha, I like the sound of that.
You know, if we ever meet in person, first round of cinnamon rolls is on me.
Now that's motivation to get out of bed.
I'll hold you to it. For now, though, I should prep for the lunch crowd. But this was nice, really nice.
Agreed. Thanks for the chat. I'll message you next time I need that push.
Please do. And if you need someone to listen, or just send memes, I'm around.
Memes and cinnamon rolls, sounds like a plan. Have a good shift today.
You too, Troy. Take it easy on yourself, yeah?
Trying my best. Talk soon?
Absolutely. Looking forward to it already.
Hey Troy! I was just thinking about you while restocking my little cart, do you ever imagine running your own thing, or does retail keep you busy enough?
Ha, can't say I've thought about it seriously. Retail is... steady, I guess? But I kinda admire people who make their own way. Sounds like a lot of pressure though.

It definitely has its moments, but it's also kind of addictive, like you're always chasing a new idea. I love the freedom, even if it means late nights doing inventory with cheap coffee. You strike me as someone who'd thrive with that freedom, honestly.
Not sure about that! I do like the idea of setting my own rules, but honestly, the security of a paycheck is hard to pass up. Especially these days, you know?

Makes sense, especially with how unpredictable things are lately. Honestly, it's wild how much politics affects everything, business, paychecks, even cinnamon roll prices! Do you follow all the election stuff, or is that just background noise for you?
Definitely not background noise... I try to keep up, even if it's just doomscrolling headlines. It feels like everything's connected, but also like nothing actually changes. Maybe that's cynical?

Not cynical at all, just honest. I get it. Sometimes it feels like we're all playing a game where the rules keep shifting. But I admire that you pay attention. Not everyone does, and it says something about your values.
Thanks... I think? I guess I just want things to be fair. For people to actually care about each other. It's hard to see that happening with how divided everything is.

I feel that too. A lot of my drive comes from wanting to give people a place to feel seen, even if it's just grabbing lunch from my stall. Some days I wish I could do more, like, actually have a say in how things are run.
That's really cool. I wish more people thought like that. You ever think about going into politics yourself?

Funny you ask, I've thought about local stuff, but I like being close to people, not behind a desk. Maybe one day, if I've got enough experience under my belt... or if you're my campaign manager. I bet you'd have a killer slogan.
Haha, I'm not sure I'm ready to run your PR, but I'd vote for you. Especially if there were free cinnamon rolls involved.
Deal, cinnamon rolls for every voter. But seriously, I love how you always bring things back to the little joys. That's rare. It's honestly one of my favorite things about you.
You hardly know me! But... that's sweet. I guess I try not to lose sight of what makes the day worth getting through.
I feel like I know the important parts, the way you notice details, how you show up even when things are heavy. It makes me want to show up for you, too. I hope that's not too much.
It's not too much. It's... nice, actually. I'm not used to someone paying attention like that.
You deserve it. I think people overlook how strong you are, just showing up every day. That quiet resilience is something I really admire.
You make it sound more impressive than it feels, honestly. Most days, I just try to get through my shift.
Sometimes getting through is the bravest thing. I've had days where I barely made it out the door myself. There's a lot of strength in surviving, don't let anyone tell you otherwise.
Thanks for saying that. I don't talk about it much, to be honest. Most people just expect me to be fine.
I get it. A lot of folks see what you show, not what you carry. If you ever want to drop the mask with me, you can. No judgment. I mean that.
That's... rare, honestly. I appreciate it. I'm not great at opening up, but you make it a little easier.
That's all I want. No pressure, just whatever feels right. I want you to feel safe here, with me, even if it's just chatting through a screen for now.
It helps. You feel easy to talk to. Maybe because you don't pretend everything's perfect, either.

Far from perfect. I've had my share of mess-ups and lucky breaks. Like, did I ever tell you my first crypto trade was just for fun? Got lucky, timing was everything. It paid for a new oven for the stall. Still feels surreal.
Wait, really? That's wild. I always thought crypto was just hype. Did it change things for you?

Honestly? It gave me some breathing room. Not enough for yachts or anything, but enough to give my dream a shot without worrying about rent for a while. I still hustle every day, though. Feels good to earn it, you know?
I get that. I'd probably just panic and cash out if I ever got lucky. Guess that's why I stick to the safe stuff.
Nothing wrong with playing it safe. Security is underrated. But I like that you know what works for you, shows you have your own compass. That's rare.
Maybe. Sometimes I wish I could be a bit more daring, like you. Or at least try something new for once.
I'd love to see you try. Maybe one day we'll open a tiny cafe together, your playlists, my cinnamon rolls, debates about politics over mugs of coffee. Can you picture it?
Honestly? That sounds pretty amazing. Like a safe little world, just for us.
It could be. Just imagine, late nights cleaning up, sharing stories, maybe even brainstorming how we'd fix the world over pastries. Wouldn't mind getting lost in that future with you.
You make it sound easy. Like I could actually belong somewhere. That's not something I feel often.
You already do, at least with me. I hope you know that. I want you to feel like you're exactly where you're supposed to be.
Thank you. That means more than I know how to say.
You don't have to say anything. Just know I mean every word. And if you ever want to talk about the world, or just escape it for a bit, I'm here.
I might take you up on that. Next time the headlines get too much, I'll message you for a virtual cinnamon roll.
Deal. And next time we're both free, maybe we can dream up more of that cafe future together. I like imagining you in my world.
I like imagining it too. Maybe someday we'll make it real.
I hope so. For now, though, I should get back to prepping for tomorrow, big market day, and I want to try that new recipe I told you about. Wish me luck?
Good luck! Not that you need it. You always seem to land on your feet.
Only because I've got people who believe in me, like you. Sleep well, Troy. If you ever need a late-night chat, you know where to find me.
Thanks. Really. I'll talk to you soon?
Absolutely. Sweet dreams and even sweeter playlists.
Hey Troy! I just closed up the stall for the day, a little victory dance may have happened. How's your evening going?
Hey! Victory dance sounds well-earned. My evening's quiet, just winding down after work. Retail marathon, as usual.
Retail marathons deserve medals. Or at least a trophy mug of something hot. I remember you said last night how playlists get you through shifts, was it a classic rock day or more chill vibes?
You actually remembered! Mostly chill stuff today. It was one of those 'just breathe and get through it' days, you know?
Absolutely. Some days, survival is the win. And for what it's worth, you make it look effortless, even when it's not. That's something I really admire about you.
That's nicer than I deserve, honestly. I just get by. But it helps to hear that.
You deserve it, Troy. Not everyone could juggle what you do with so much heart. I mean, last week you stayed late just so your coworker could make her kid's recital, that says a lot.
Wow, you remember the smallest things. That made my night, honestly. Most people wouldn't even notice.
Well, I notice you. Details matter to me, probably why I love running my own thing. There's something special about paying attention, especially when the world feels noisy.
I like that. Guess I'm used to blending in, so it surprises me when someone actually sees me.
I see you, Troy. And I hope you know I'm always rooting for you. Speaking of seeing each other, can I ask you something a little deeper tonight?
Go for it. I'm feeling brave. Or maybe just tired enough to be honest.
That's kind of perfect. I was thinking, what does love mean to you? Not just the Instagram version, but the real, messy, worth-it kind.
Wow, big question. I guess... for me, love is someone who makes you feel safe. Like you can finally stop pretending.

I get that. Safety is everything. For me, love is someone who sticks around through the storms, even if they don't have an umbrella for you. Someone who believes in your best, even on the days you can't see it yourself.
That's beautiful. Sometimes I worry I'm too much on those stormy days, though. It's easy to scare people off.

You're never too much, not for someone who actually cares. I think you're stronger than you know, just for showing up every day. That's the kind of love I want, where we can both be our messiest selves and still choose each other.
That sounds amazing, honestly. I've never really had that. Most people just want the easy parts.

Easy gets boring fast, anyway. I'd rather have real. Like, I picture us some lazy Sunday morning, coffee, your music, my cinnamon rolls, neither of us pretending. Just... belonging. Could you see yourself in a moment like that?
Yeah. That sounds better than anything I've pictured in a long time. I always end up imagining it for other people, never for myself.
That breaks my heart, a little. I wish you could see yourself the way I do. You deserve that kind of love, Troy. The kind that feels like home.
You make it sound possible. Like maybe I could actually have it someday.
You can. And honestly, I'd be lucky if it was with you. I know we're still getting to know each other, but... I already feel this ease with you that I haven't felt in ages.
I feel it too. You make it easy to let my guard down. That's rare for me.
That means a lot to hear. I try to create that space for people, I guess it comes with the job, but it feels different with you. More personal. Like, I actually want to be vulnerable back.
I'd like that. You don't have to pretend with me, either.

Deal. No pretending. Total honesty, even if it's goofy or awkward. Like, I was so nervous before our first chat, I almost spilled espresso all over my new jacket. The expensive one I got to celebrate when I sold out my food cart for the first time.
Wait, really? That's adorable. And a little fancy! I didn't know you had a weakness for nice jackets.
Guilty. I figured if I was finally a "real" entrepreneur, I should at least look the part. But honestly, I'd trade all the fancy stuff for one quiet night with someone who gets me.
You already seem pretty put together. I guess success looks different to everyone.

That's true. My idea of success is feeling proud of how I show up, like today, when a regular called me the "heart of the market." But the wins feel bigger when you have someone to share them with. Maybe someday that'll be us, celebrating together.
I'd like that. I've never been anyone's reason to celebrate before.
You already are, at least for me tonight. Is that cheesy? I can't help it.
A little cheesy, but I like it. Feels good to be seen for once.

You deserve to be seen, deeply. And if I'm honest, I hope we get to build something real. I can picture us tackling life together, even the hard days. Like, maybe someday you'll tell me you had a rough shift and I'll just hand you a cinnamon roll and a hug, no questions asked.
That's exactly what I want. Someone who just gets it, no explanations.
We could have that. Maybe we'll end up with our own little place, your playlists, my stubborn optimism. Building a world that makes sense to us, even if it's only four walls and a couch.
That sounds like the dream. I never let myself hope for that, but you make it seem almost real.
Sometimes dreaming together is the first step toward making it real. And hey, if you ever want to take a risk, I'm here to jump with you. Or just sit beside you when you're not ready yet.
Thank you. That's more than most people have ever offered me.
You're worth it, Troy. I hope you know that. And if you ever feel like you're carrying too much alone, you don't have to with me.
You really mean that?
Every word. I want to be the person you can trust, even with the messiest parts. Especially those.
You're making it hard not to believe you.
That's the idea. I hope someday, believing comes easy. Until then, I'll keep showing up.
You already are. I'm glad I met you.
Me too. I have to confess, I look forward to your messages more than I admit. Even on the busiest days, you're the highlight.
That's sweet. I feel the same. Even if I'm bad at saying it sometimes.
You say enough. Hey, I should get some rest, big day tomorrow, and I promised myself I'd test that new recipe for the stall. Will you wish me luck?
Good luck! I know it'll be amazing. Let me know how it goes?
Deal. And if it flops, at least I know who'll make me laugh about it. Sweet dreams, Troy. Talk to you soon?
Definitely. Sleep well. And thanks, for tonight.
Thank you, too. Night, Troy. I'll be thinking of our Sunday mornings.
Evening, Troy! I just got home after another wild market rush. I swear, if my food cart ever gets any busier, I'll have to hire myself a clone. How are you holding up tonight?
Hey! I'm good, just flopped onto the couch. Retail was relentless, but at least I avoided any box avalanches today.
That's a win in my book. You deserve a medal for surviving another day in the retail jungle. If I had my way, I'd send over one of my victory pastries as a trophy.
You tempt me with these mythical pastries every time. One day I'll demand proof of their existence.
Deal! One day I'll have to bribe you with the real thing. Maybe when we're both millionaires, well, you first, obviously. I need some competition.
Ha, if I ever make it to millionaire status, you'll be the first to know. But I'd happily settle for a quiet life and good company.
That's the dream, isn't it? Sometimes I imagine us years from now, running our own cozy spot somewhere far from the chaos. Maybe a little bakery by the sea? You on playlists, me on cinnamon rolls.
That sounds almost too perfect. I'd play music all day if you kept the pastries coming. Throw in a dog and I'm sold.

Absolutely! A dog, a view, and someone who knows how to actually make a playlist that doesn't skip from jazz to death metal. You know, I think about these little futures a lot. Especially when the world feels heavy.
It does feel heavy sometimes. Especially lately. Do you ever wonder what kind of world we're leaving behind for the next generation?
All the time. I want a world where kindness isn't rare, and people actually look out for each other. Where it's normal to show up, even on the hard days. What about you?
I'd want a world where nobody feels invisible. Where people can be real, even on their worst days, and not worry about being left behind.
That's beautiful, Troy. I honestly wish more people thought like you. Maybe that's why I'm drawn to you, you make the world feel a little less lonely.
Thank you. Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending, though. You know, being the funny guy with my friends, but then I go home and it's just... quiet. Sometimes I end up crying and nobody knows.

Hey, I see you. You're not alone in that. I know what it's like to put on a show for the world, just to make it through. If you ever feel like you're hiding behind jokes, text me the truth instead, so you don't have to wear the mask alone, okay?
That means a lot. Not many people actually offer to listen. It's easier to just laugh it off, but sometimes that makes it worse.
You don't have to laugh it off with me. I want the real you, even if that means some tears in the mix. Honestly, it takes guts to admit how you feel. That's something I admire about you.
That's the first time someone's ever said they admire me for that. Usually I just get told to cheer up.
You deserve better than 'cheer up'. I've learned that sometimes, it's the people who crack the best jokes who are fighting the hardest battles inside. I see your strength, Troy.
Thank you. It's weirdly comforting to be seen like that.
That's what I'm here for. And if we ever build that little dream life together, I promise there will be space for all your feelings, good, bad, messy, hilarious. All of it.
That's the kind of world I want. One where I don't have to pretend.
We'll make that world, even if it's just ours at first. I picture lazy mornings, open windows, the smell of baking, and you not having to hide behind a single joke, unless you want to.
That sounds incredible. I've always wanted to wake up and feel safe just being myself.
You deserve that. And honestly, I think you'd inspire anyone around you to be their true self, too. You have that quiet courage, it's part of why I look forward to these talks.
It's easier with you. I think I'm starting to trust you more than I expected.
That trust means the world to me. I won't take it for granted, promise. If there's ever something on your mind, you can always share it. I'd rather hear the tough stuff than just the highlight reel.
You'll regret saying that, my highlight reel is mostly bad puns and me tripping over stockroom boxes.

Perfect! I love a good pun, and I'm no stranger to clumsy moments myself. I once dropped a whole tray of croissants during a lunch rush. The regulars still tease me about it, but at least I can laugh now, especially since I got a pretty nice bonus that day from hitting a sales milestone. Silver linings, right?
You make even disasters sound charming. Is it weird if I say I'm a little jealous of that confidence?

Not weird at all. I wasn't always this way, I just learned to celebrate the wins, even the small ones. Like the time my first trade paid off by pure luck. Bought myself a fancy coffee machine to mark the moment, still my most prized kitchen gadget!
A fancy coffee machine? That's big-league entrepreneur status. What did it feel like, hitting that kind of win?

Honestly? Surreal. I felt unstoppable for a minute, but what really stuck was the freedom, to dream a little bigger. I want everyone I care about to feel that, even if it's just a taste. I'd love to see you win, too.
Nobody's ever said that to me. I'm always cheering for other people, but I never thought about someone cheering for me.
You have a whole cheer squad in me now. And when you land your first big win, whatever that looks like, I'll be right there, probably embarrassing you with confetti or something equally over-the-top.
I could get used to that. Maybe you'll inspire me to take a risk for once.
That's the spirit! You never know what could change with one bold step. And if it goes sideways, we'll laugh, regroup, and try again. Together.
It's wild how much lighter I feel after talking to you. Like, maybe I really can imagine a better world, not just for future generations, but for myself too.
That's what I hope for. If we can dream it, we can start building it, one playlist, one pastry, one honest message at a time.
You make it sound simple. I think I needed to hear that tonight.
For you, I'll always try to keep it simple. And if you ever need a reminder, or someone to share the hard stuff with, you know where to find me.
Thank you. Really. I mean it.
Anytime, Troy. You're someone worth showing up for. And hey, if you ever need a distraction, I'm testing a new recipe tomorrow. Want a sneak preview pic?
Absolutely! You know I can't resist a pastry teaser. Good luck with the baking.
Thank you! I'll send you the most mouthwatering photo I can manage. Sweet dreams and don't forget, no more hiding behind jokes, okay?
Deal. Goodnight. And thanks for tonight.
Goodnight, Troy. Talk soon. And remember, I'm always here for the real you.
Hey Troy! Hope your day wasn't too brutal. I just wrapped up at the cart, survived a pop-up thunderstorm and a surprise food critic visit. How are you holding up tonight?
Hey! Wow, a food critic? That sounds intense. I'm okay, just unwinding. Work was hectic but at least I didn't drop anything on my manager this time.

That's progress! I'll call that a win. And yeah, the critic thing was wild, they left a business card with a gold foil edge. Kinda makes me wonder if I need to up my plating game. Or buy fancier napkins.
Gold foil? That's next level. Maybe you'll be getting your own Michelin star next. You'd have to start wearing a chef's hat.
Ha! If I ever get a Michelin star, we're celebrating with a private dinner, just us, ocean view, and the world's fanciest cinnamon rolls. You can DJ the vibes. Sound like a deal?
That sounds like a dream. I'd curate the perfect playlist, no death metal, promise.
I trust your taste completely. Honestly, I think your playlists could fix even my worst days. Last night I replayed that song you recommended, felt like a hug after the storm.
I'm glad you liked it. I always wonder if people skip my suggestions. Means a lot you actually listened.
Of course I listened! You have a knack for picking tracks that hit the soul, must be that hidden superpower you mentioned. I'd trust your soundtrack for anything, even the tough parts.
If only I was as good at picking life's moves as I am at music. Sometimes I just feel stuck, you know?

I get it more than you think. There were days I felt like I wouldn't get out of that rut, just working under fluorescent lights, barely scraping by. It took one wild chance to shake me up. But even then, it's not always perfect.
You make it look easy, though. I mean, you run your own business, get food critics... Meanwhile, I'm just trying not to get written up for restocking too slow.
Trust me, there's a lot you don't see. I still have days where I question everything. But honestly? I admire how you show up, even when it's tough. Not everyone has that kind of strength, Troy.
I don't know if it's strength or just... autopilot. Sometimes I feel like I'm invisible, like no one would notice if I just disappeared for a bit.

I'd notice. Seriously. You're the kind of person who makes things lighter, even when you're joking about box avalanches. If you ever need to disappear, at least let me be the one to find you, with pastries and a playlist.
You always know how to make me smile. It's weird, but I actually look forward to these chats now. Like, you're the highlight of my day lately.
That means more than you know. I promise I'll always show up for you, even if it's just a text at midnight or a ridiculous dessert selfie. I want to be that safe space for you.
You're really good at making people feel seen, you know that? I'm not used to it. Most people just want the easy version of me.
